APPEAL No. 882 of 2013  SMT. RANJANA AND 5 ORS. AND OTHERS  Versus  SIDDHANT KUMAR AND 2 ORS. AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Manish Sujan Jain, learned counsel for the app  Shri Pradip Kumar Gupta, learned counsel for the re  ORDER

sentences.text: With the consent of learned counsel for the parties the matter is finally heard.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants/claimants being aggrieved by the award dated 27.7.2012 passed in Claim Case No.97/2011 by 10th Additional MACT, Ujjain,whereby a total sum of Rs.17,91,200/- has been awarded to them by way of compensation.

2. As per the appellants on 25.12.2010 at about 1.00 AM deceased Jivaji Rao, who was husband of appellant No.1, father of appellants No.2 to 4 and son of appellants No.5 to 6 had gone to Ghonsla at Kota-Ujjain Road on account of accident having occurred therein since he was a Police Head Constable.
During course of his duty he was crossing the road.

At that time respondent No.2 drove vehicle bearing registration No.RJ-20-YA-0687, which was owned by respondent No.1 and was insured with respondent No.3 rashly and negligently and dashed the same against the deceased as a result of which he suffered injuries.

He was taken NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:9325 2 MA-882-2013 to hospital, but eventually expired.
3. The appellants then filed application under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 before the claims Tribunal for award of a sum of Rs.31,53,510/- to them by way of compensation.

The application was Smt. Ranjana And 5 Ors. vs Siddhant Kumar And 2 Ors. on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168398743/
1 contested by the respondents by filing their written statement.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the written statement respondent No.3 inter alia contended that the accident occurred as a result of contributory negligence of the deceased.

After evaluation of evidence brought on record by the parties the claims Tribunal determined the total amount of compensation at Rs.22,23,936/-, but further recorded a finding that the deceased had also contributed to the accident to the extent of 20%, therefore, compensation as aforesaid has been awarded to the appellants.
4. This appeal has been preferred by the appellants on the ground that the finding of the claims Tribunal as regards contributory negligence of the deceased towards accident is perverse.
The eye-witness Salim Baig has categorically stated that the deceased had looked properly and had thereafter only crossed the road.

The accident had occurred when he had almost crossed the road,
hence it could not have been held that there was any contributory negligence on his part.
The statement of the Driver of the offending vehicle also affirms the said fact.

It is further submitted that while determining the amount of compensation future prospects of rise in income have not been taken into consideration by the claims Tribunal, which were mandatorily required to be considered.
It is further submitted that the amount of compensation determined requires to be enhanced and they may be awarded just compensation in its entirety.

5. Learned counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance Company submits that finding of the Tribunal as regards contributory negligence of the deceased is NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:9325 3 MA-882-2013 perfectly just and reasoned and based on the evidence available on record, which has been scanned in its proper perspective by the claims Tribunal.
The incident occurred in the night at about 1.00 AM when it was quite easy to see any car approaching from a long distance.
The width of the road was also not much.
If the deceased had exercised due diligence the accident could have been avoided, but he did not do so, hence he is liable for contributory negligence towards the accident.

It is also submitted that amount of compensation determined and awarded to the appellants is just and proper in which no interference is warranted in view of which the appeal deserves to be dismissed.
6. I have considered the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.
7. Salim Baig (AW-3) is the eye-witness of the incident.
He had stated that when the deceased was crossing the road driver of the offending vehicle drove the same in rash and negligent manner and dashed the deceased in which he suffered grievous injuries.
In his cross-examination he further deposed that prior to crossing the road deceased had looked left and right and had thereafter only crossed the road.
When the accident occurred he had almost crossed the road and only 4-5 feet of the same was remaining.
From his statement it is evident that the deceased was crossing the road by taking due care and caution and had exercised the due diligence as would have been expected from a prudent man.
The fact that the entire road had been crossed by him leads to conclusion that there was no negligence on his part.

The Driver of the offending vehicle Surajmal Bunkar in his cross-examination has expressed total unawareness of the incident and stated that he did not see the deceased crossing the road and only heard a noise after which he stopped his vehicle and saw that the deceased had been hit by him.
This itself shows that he was absolutely negligent in driving the vehicle.
From the evidence NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9325 4 MA-882-2013 Smt. Ranjana And 5 Ors. vs Siddhant Kumar And 2 Ors.

sentences.text:
on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168398743/
2 available on record it is categorically proved that the accident had occurred due to negligence of the driver and there was no contribution of the deceased towards the accident.
The claims Tribunal has erred in holding that the deceased was also responsible for the accident, hence the finding as regards his contributory negligence is set aside.
8. The income of the deceased which has been determined by the claims Tribunal is correct.

However, the future prospects of rise in income which are mandatorily required to be taken into consideration as per the decision of Hon'ble Apex court in the case of National Insurance Co.Ltd.,
Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, 2017 ACJ 2700 SC , have not been taken into consideration by the claims Tribunal.

sentences.text: In view of the age of the deceased the same ought to be taken at 30%.

Moreover, as per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram, 2019 ACJ SC 2782, the appellants are also entitled for award of filial consortium but the claims Tribunal has totally ignored the said aspect and has not awarded any amount to the appellants on that count.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram, 2019 ACJ SC 2782
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The amount of funeral expenses awarded are also low and no amount has been awarded towards loss of estate.

9. For future loss of income the appellants are entitled for a sum of Rs.19,008/- per month x 12 +
30%, which would be Rs.2,96,524.80.
The dependency of 3/4th taken and the multiplier of 13 adopted by the claims Tribunal is correct.
For future loss of income the appellants are entitled for Rs.28,91,116.80.
For filial consortium they are entitled for Rs.2,40,000/- since they are six in number.

For funeral expenses and loss of estate they deserve to be awarded a sum of Rs.15,000/-
each.

10. The appellants are entitled for total sum of Rs.31,61,116.80 by way of compensation, whereas the claims Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.17,91,200/-
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9325 5 MA-882-2013 only to them.

The appellants are held entitled for enhancement in the amount of compensation by a sum of Rs.13,69,916.80, which shall be paid to them alongwith interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of the claim application till the date of its realization.
11. The appellants have valued their appeal at Rs.7,00,000/-.
They are liable to pay Court fees on the enhanced amount of Rs.9,22,181/- in view of the findings as recorded above.
They are, hence directed to pay the requisite Court fees on the remaining amount of Rs.2,22,181/- within a period of two months from today.
In case of their failure to pay the Court fees as aforesaid, the amount of Rs.2,22,181/- shall cease to carry any interest after a period of two months.
12. The appeal is accordingly partly allowed and disposed off.
